summary: Implement the provider-neutral fail-closed approval engine with immutable versioned policies, staged quorum/four-eyes/scope evidence, expiry/escalation, execution lifecycle, forced-RLS persistence and atomic audit/outbox evidence.

impacts.evidence: Policies, requests, decisions and escalation evidence are organization/workspace owned with composite foreign keys, transaction-local tenant scope and forced RLS. Cross-tenant policy/request evidence cannot be selected or mutated by the application role.

Approval evidence stores bounded identifiers, scopes, state and sanitized comments only. Raw provider payloads and credentials are excluded; secret-shaped comments are replaced with the canonical redaction marker.
Three additive Draft 2020-12 approval contracts are introduced. Existing OpenAPI approval listing remains compatible and no published request/response field is removed or renamed.

Five additive governance.approval.*.v1 event payloads are registered. Existing event types and payload schemas are unchanged, and all new events are emitted through the canonical Transactional Outbox envelope.

Connector SDK v1 root interfaces, plugin security, sandbox and conformance contracts are unchanged. Connectors remain ordinary callers of host approval policy and cannot implement provider-specific bypasses.

Expand migration 000013 adds four new approval tables, indexes, forced RLS and defensive triggers without renaming/dropping existing columns or tables. Historical policy/decision/escalation evidence is append-oriented.

Sensitive and legally-significant writes deny without matching active policy. Four-eyes, eligible scopes, stage quorum, exact policy version, expiry and allowed state transitions are enforced in Go and PostgreSQL; direct SQL cannot forge final approval without decision evidence.

Task 017 becomes the canonical risk-to-approval boundary: read/write-safe may allow, sensitive/legal writes fail closed without policy and otherwise require versioned multi-stage approval before execution.

Policy install, request, decision, escalation and execution transitions append safe audit records in the same transaction as state and outbox intent. Task 030 will add cross-domain lineage/timeline reads using these stable request/policy identifiers.

Optimistic request versions, unique actor vote per stage and caller-supplied immutable audit/event IDs make retries fail closed rather than double-apply approval state. Downstream sensitive execution still uses its normal Inbox/Outbox/idempotency boundary.
Task 017 adds no webhook transport or direct external egress. Approval events remain internal EventBus facts; Task 063 owns durable outbound webhooks.

Stable states, escalation count, UTC deadlines and normalized failure codes provide bounded metrics for pending age, expiry, approval latency and execution outcomes without persisting arbitrary remote error text.

The migration is additive. Rollback of binaries leaves immutable approval evidence intact; policy/request tables must not be dropped as an emergency rollback because historical authorization evidence is auditable state.

Tests cover fail-closed risk gating, four-eyes, scope eligibility, staged quorum, duplicate votes, rejection, expiry, escalation, execution binding and secret-comment redaction; migration audits assert forced RLS, append-only evidence and DB quorum guards.
